newsitem.title: RWANDA: UN asks Zaire to allow hunt for "lost" refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN asks Zaire to allow hunt for "lost" refugees.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency on Sunday asked Zaire's government to allow it to carry out an aerial search for some 30,000 Rwandan refugees who have disappeared from a camp at Kalima, south of Kisangani.
Missionaries near Kalima, contacted by radio from Rwanda, said they believed the town had fallen to Laurent Kabila's fighters of the Alliance of Democratic Forces.
"We believe the town has fallen," one missionary said adding that he got the information from local people in the area. The missionaries had no further details.

Arianne Quentier, spokesperson for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in eastern Zaire's largest city, Kisangani, told Reuters by telephone that there was still no sign of the refugees, who left their camp on Saturday.
The evacuation of the Kalima camp raised speculation of renewed fighting in the area between anti-government rebels, who now control large areas of eastern Zaire, and government forces.
But rebel leader Laurent Kabila, interviewed in Bukavu, Zaire, at the weekend said there had been no new fighting.
"We were trying to overfly the area this morning, but as yet we haven't got clearance," Quentier said on Sunday.

She said the refugees, who appeared to have fled a rebel advance towards their camp at Kalima, 300 km (200 miles) from Zaire's eastern border, had not shown up at the nearby towns of Kindu or Punia, where it was thought they might be headed.
"We can only believe they are somewhere in the forest," she said.

The rebels, fighting to overthrow Zaire's president of 31 years Mobutu Sese Seko, control a strip of territory over 1,000 km (600 miles) long and have begun to advance deeper towards the heart of the mineral-rich central African country.
The rebels last year overran camps housing over a million, mostly Hutu, refugees who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals following the genocide of over 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
At least 700,000 refugees returned to Rwanda last year, but others, including much of the former Rwanda army and militias, fled further into Zaire.
UNHCR information shows a trickle of displaced Zaireans moving towards Kisangani from areas northeast of the city, where the rebels are also reportedly advancing.
